questions.prompt: Who was the first woman to be awarded a Nobel Prize?
questions.fact: She went on to win a second, in a different science, and remains the only person ever to manage that.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a substance that cannot be broken down chemically?
questions.fact: Ninety-four occur naturally on Earth. Everything past those has only ever existed inside a laboratory.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum score from a single throw in darts?
questions.fact: Triple twenty is the highest single-dart score, which is why the twenty sits at the top of the board rather than the bullseye.

questions.prompt: Which video game franchise features a character called Lara Croft?
questions.fact: Her distinctive angular look was partly an accident of early hardware, which could not render smooth curves cheaply.

questions.prompt: Which strait connects the Mediterranean to the Black Sea?
questions.fact: Istanbul sits on both banks, making it the only major city in the world spanning two continents.

questions.prompt: Which author created the detective Philip Marlowe?
questions.fact: He only started writing fiction at forty-four, after losing an oil executive job during the Depression.

questions.prompt: What does the acronym IP stand for in IP address?
questions.fact: The original scheme allowed about 4.3 billion addresses, a number thought absurdly generous when it was chosen.
